title: Button
summary: A native action control with emphasis, icon, busy, grouped toggle, and responsive variants.
overview: A dependency-free button recipe built on the native button element. It keeps action semantics, keyboard behavior, focus treatment, and state announcements intact while exposing a compact token surface.

component.useWhen: Use a button to submit data or perform an action in the current interface.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid buttons for navigation to another URL; use an anchor so browser link behavior remains available.

examples.title: Action hierarchy
examples.description: Activate the primary, secondary, and quiet actions and compare them with the native disabled state.

source.html: Choose an action.

variants.title: Icon-only buttons
variants.summary: Square action buttons with inline icons, full-size hit areas, and explicit accessible names.
variants.useWhen: Use an icon-only button in a familiar, space-constrained toolbar where the symbol has a clear accessible name.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid it when the icon is unfamiliar or the action needs explanation; keep a visible text label instead.
customization: Keep the inline and block size tied to --button-control-height so the hit area never shrinks below the shared minimum.
Replace the inline SVG while retaining aria-hidden on the artwork and aria-label on the button.
Use the same primary, secondary, and quiet emphasis classes as text buttons.

example.title: Compact toolbar actions
example.description: Tab through the square controls and activate them to verify that the accessible label also drives the status message.

source.html: Choose a grouped action.

variants.title: Busy state
variants.summary: A submit-style button that prevents duplicate activation and announces progress without relying on its spinner.
variants.useWhen: Use a busy state while one bounded action is in progress and duplicate activation would be harmful or confusing.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid indefinite busy buttons for background work; use a persistent status or progress component when completion may take a long time.
customization: Call setBusy(true) before asynchronous work and setBusy(false) in a finally block in production code.
The spinner is decorative; the changing label and polite live region carry the state accessibly.
The demo timer only simulates a request and is cleared by destroy().

example.title: Save with progress feedback
example.description: Start the simulated save and verify that the button becomes disabled, its label changes, and completion is announced.

source.html: Ready to save.

variants.title: Responsive action layout
variants.summary: A dialog-style action row that becomes a full-width vertical stack on narrow screens.
variants.useWhen: Use a responsive action group when adjacent decisions fit horizontally on larger screens but need larger targets and clearer order on mobile.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid treating unrelated page actions as one group; keep each control near the content it affects.
customization: Change only the 32rem layout threshold when the labels no longer fit without wrapping.
column-reverse keeps the primary action visually first while preserving the safer secondary action first in DOM order.
Every button retains the shared 2.75rem minimum height and focus outline.

example.title: Stacked mobile actions
example.description: Switch the preview between desktop and mobile widths to see the actions move from a row to a full-width stack.

source.html: Choose how to continue.

variants.title: Button group
variants.summary: Related actions arranged as a visually connected group.
variants.useWhen: Group a small set of related actions that operate in the same context.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid grouping unrelated actions or using a toolbar role when the controls do not form a toolbar.
customization: Use role="group" with a concise accessible label for related actions.
Keep visual emphasis consistent with the action hierarchy.
Allow the group to wrap on narrow screens.

example.title: Grouped actions
example.description: Related actions presented as a connected, responsive group.

source.html: Choose an action.

variants.title: Toggle buttons
variants.summary: Connected buttons for exclusive or multiple selections, with visible pressed states and keyboard navigation.
variants.useWhen: Use grouped toggle buttons for a small set of related choices, such as text alignment or formatting.
variants.avoidWhen: Use a switch for an immediate on/off setting or a radio group when a form choice must always have one selected value.
customization: Set data-toggle-group to exclusive for one-or-none selection, or multiple for independent pressed states.
Give every icon button a stable aria-label and keep aria-pressed synchronized with its visual state.
Keep one tab stop per group. Arrow keys, Home, and End move focus without changing selection; Enter or Space activates the focused button.
The selected state uses the shared --button-accent and --button-accent-text tokens.

example.title: Alignment and formatting
example.description: Choose one alignment or turn several formatting options on and off. Use arrow keys within each group and activate with Enter or Space.

anatomy.name: Native control
anatomy.description: A button element that supplies action semantics and Enter/Space activation.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Visible action-oriented text, or an accessible name when the control contains only an icon.

anatomy.name: Optional icon
anatomy.description: Decorative inline artwork that reinforces the label without replacing it.

anatomy.name: State feedback
anatomy.description: Disabled, busy, focus, and pressed styling that remains distinguishable without color alone.

tokens.name: --button-accent
tokens.description: Primary action background and focus-support color.

tokens.name: --button-accent-text
tokens.description: Text and icon color on primary actions.

tokens.name: --button-control-height
tokens.description: Minimum button height and icon-button width.

accessibility: Use a native button for actions and an anchor with href for navigation.
Always set type="button" unless the control intentionally submits or resets its form.
Give icon-only controls a concise aria-label or aria-labelledby value.
Keep visible focus, a minimum 2.75rem target, and text that communicates destructive or consequential actions directly.
Expose asynchronous work with aria-busy and a live text update; never rely on animation alone.
Use the native disabled attribute only when the control should leave the tab order.
component.responsive: Buttons wrap without clipping. The responsive-actions variant becomes a full-width vertical stack below 32rem while preserving a logical DOM and keyboard order.
limitations: The basic recipe reports activation only; application-specific commands, form submission, and error handling remain the consumer's responsibility.
Inline SVG icons are intentionally simple and should be replaced with product-approved artwork while preserving their accessible naming contract.

provenance.label: Native button patterns informed by Material UI
provenance.note: Original native HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The grouped selection behavior is informed by the Material UI Toggle Button documentation; no library source is copied.
